definitions.explanation: Microscopic single-celled organisms. Used in both scientific contexts and everyday language when talking about hygiene, illness, and food safety.

examples.japanese: {細菌|さいきん}が{繁殖|はんしょく}する。
{手|て}を{洗|あら}わないと{細菌|さいきん}がつく。
examples.english: If you don't wash your hands, germs will get on them.

examples.japanese: この{食中毒|しょくちゅうどく}は{細菌|さいきん}が{原因|げんいん}だと{判明|はんめい}した。
examples.english: It was determined that bacteria were the cause of this food poisoning.

notes:
USAGE:
A technical term used in both scientific and everyday contexts. Unlike the homophone {最近|さいきん} (recently), this word is written with different kanji and belongs to a completely different semantic field.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {細菌|さいきん}が{繁殖|はんしょく}する: bacteria multiply
- {細菌|さいきん}に{感染|かんせん}する: to be infected with bacteria
- {細菌|さいきん}{検査|けんさ}: bacterial testing
- {細菌|さいきん}を{殺|ころ}す: to kill germs

SIMILAR WORDS:
ウイルス (virus) refers to a different type of pathogen. {細菌|さいきん} are living organisms that can be treated with antibiotics, whereas ウイルス cannot.
